planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis or arbor; unlike Hayward, Jenny is self-fertile and does not require a separate male pollinizer vine.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, training the vigorous vine onto a sturdy trellis or arbor system able to support its weight for decades. Jenny is a self-fertile fuzzy kiwifruit selection, a genuine practical advantage over the classic Hayward variety, which requires a separate non-fruiting male vine purely for pollination — Jenny produces a crop from a single plant, making it a far more space-efficient choice for smaller home gardens that can't accommodate two full-sized kiwi vines. Fruit is somewhat smaller than Hayward and yields are generally lighter without a dedicated pollinizer nearby, but a nearby male vine (of Jenny or another compatible variety) will still improve fruit set and size if space allows. Prune annually in the dormant season to control the vine's naturally vigorous, sprawling growth and keep fruiting wood productive.

common_name: Blake Kiwi (Compact Self-Fertile California Fuzzy Kiwifruit)

planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis or arbor; self-fertile and does not require a separate male pollinizer vine.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, training the vine onto a sturdy trellis or arbor. Blake was bred in California as a self-fertile fuzzy kiwifruit with a somewhat more compact, manageable growth habit than the very vigorous Hayward, making it a practical choice for home gardeners with limited space who still want to grow classic fuzzy-skinned kiwifruit without dedicating room to a separate non-fruiting male vine. Fruit is smaller than Hayward but has good flavor, and the self-fertile trait means a single plant can produce a crop, though yields improve somewhat with a nearby pollinizer if space allows. Prune annually during dormancy to manage vine growth and maintain productive fruiting wood, and provide sturdy, long-term support, since kiwi vines are heavy and long-lived.

common_name: Saanichton 12 Kiwi (Cold-Hardy British Columbia Fuzzy Kiwifruit)

planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis; a female selection requiring a male pollinizer vine planted nearby with overlapping bloom time.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, training the vine onto a sturdy trellis, and plant a compatible male pollinizer vine nearby, since Saanichton 12 is a female-only selection that will not set fruit without cross-pollination. Bred at the Saanichton research station on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, this fuzzy kiwifruit selection was developed for improved cold hardiness and reliable ripening in cooler coastal climates than typical California-bred kiwi varieties tolerate well, extending fuzzy kiwi growing into marginal regions. Fruit quality is good, comparable to standard fuzzy kiwifruit, once pollination is properly managed with a nearby male vine. Prune annually during dormancy to control vigorous vine growth and maintain productive fruiting wood.

common_name: Matua Kiwi (Male Pollinizer for Fuzzy Kiwifruit)

planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis; a male-only vine grown purely to pollinate nearby female fuzzy kiwi vines such as Hayward and does not itself produce fruit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, training the vine onto a sturdy trellis positioned to pollinate nearby female fuzzy kiwi vines. Matua is a New Zealand-bred male fuzzy kiwi selection grown exclusively to provide pollen for female vines like Hayward, which cannot set fruit without a compatible male nearby, since kiwifruit plants are dioecious with separate male and female vines. Matua blooms relatively early and vigorously, and one male vine can typically pollinate several female vines when well positioned within the planting, making efficient use of garden space for the non-fruiting pollinizer. Because Matua itself never produces fruit, prune it primarily to encourage abundant flower production and to keep its size manageable relative to the fruiting female vines it supports.

common_name: Tomuri Kiwi (Late-Blooming Male Pollinizer for Fuzzy Kiwifruit)

planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis; a male-only vine grown purely to pollinate nearby female fuzzy kiwi vines and does not itself produce fruit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, training the vine onto a sturdy trellis positioned to pollinate nearby female fuzzy kiwi vines. Tomuri is a New Zealand-bred male fuzzy kiwi selection notable for blooming later than Matua, making it a useful complementary pollinizer planted alongside Matua to extend the overlap with female Hayward bloom across a longer window and improve overall pollination reliability, since kiwi bloom timing between individual vines can vary from year to year with weather. As with all male kiwi vines, Tomuri itself never sets fruit, existing solely to provide pollen for female vines. Prune to encourage strong, abundant flowering and to keep the vine's size proportional to the fruiting female vines it services within the planting.
